Gordito, the world’s oldest recorded giant otter, has died of natural causes at Longleat Safari Park in England, aged 19 years, 7 months and 10 days. He leaves more than 100 descendants in European zoos.

The park announced his death on November 20, 2026. His age record was verified by the Zoological Information Management System.

Gordito and his longtime mate, Iny, supported European breeding and conservation efforts for the endangered species, with an estimated 1,000 to 5,000 remaining in the wild. Reunited at Longleat in 2019, they were featured on the BBC series Animal Park.

His brother Maldito, who lives in Germany, is now the oldest living giant otter, according to Longleat staff.

⚡️ Tehran’s transport expansion continues despite US-Israeli attacks: Official

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Tehran has continued expanding its public transport network despite US-Israeli attacks on Iran, says head of Tehran’s City Council Mehdi Chamran.

Speaking at the 2026 International Municipal Forum in Moscow on Tuesday, Chamran said the city had more than 500 electric buses in operation and planned to purchase another 2,500. He also cited a contract with China for the production of 1,181 metro carriages.
​
Chamran said Tehran currently operated around 3,600 buses and 1,500 metro carriages, serving a daytime population of about 12 million. Public transport accounts for around 30% of passenger journeys, he added.
​
He said the transfer of two Chinese-built metro train sets had been halted following the start of US and Israeli attacks on Iran, while domestic production of metro trains had also begun.
​
Tehran’s City Council signed a cooperation memorandum with Moscow’s City Duma. Chamran said Tehran could benefit from Moscow's experience in smart urban management, digital services, crisis management and alternative urban financing models.
